mechanism_narrative: The sustained collapse in WORKPLACES mobility, together with still-negative TRANSIT, implies fewer weekday trips that convert into retail visits. If office attendance does not recover, RETAIL_REC stays below its last-four-week mean over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior four-week mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain at or below their current levels for four consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS jumps back above +45 while WORKPLACES remains near zero or negative, discretionary out-of-home time shifts toward leisure and away from retail errands. That substitution lowers RETAIL_REC within the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses above +45 week-on-week while WORKPLACES stays below 0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week after PARKS crosses above +45 while WORKPLACES remains below 0.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in GROCERY_PHARM indicates more necessity trips are being completed locally, reducing bundled shopping and spillover retail visits. Over two weeks, that pattern keeps RETAIL_REC from recovering.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM staying at or above its current level.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp PARKS rebound above its recent trend signals weather- or season-driven outdoor substitution away from indoor retail and recreation. If PARKS remains elevated for four weeks, RETAIL_REC will stay below its prior four-week average.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above its recent 2-week average by at least 20 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though PARKS stays at least 20 points above its recent two-week average.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT begins recovering while WORKPLACES is still sharply negative, the transit rebound reflects travel normalization before shopping demand returns. That lagged commute recovery should produce a short-run increase in retail visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises for two consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES remains below -5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-two-week mean within 14 days after TRANSIT rises for two consecutive weeks and WORKPLACES stays below -5.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility keeps falling toward baseline while WORKPLACES remains negative, more residents spend time out of home but not at work, which favors local discretionary shopping. This should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week mean for the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL trends downward and WORKPLACES stays negative.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES rises above -10 and TRANSIT also improves, the combined commuting network is recovering enough to generate more retail stops before and after work. That should raise RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES crosses above -10 and TRANSIT turns upward in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase above its prior four-week mean within 28 days after WORKPLACES crosses above -10 and TRANSIT turns upward.

mechanism_narrative: In a holiday-shopping regime, an upward move in GROCERY_PHARM together with stable-to-rising TRANSIT signals general trip generation that spills into retail errands. The effect appears within one week and lifts RETAIL_REC.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the week after GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT both hold at or above their current levels.
